newsitem.title: USA: Mentor says in bladder cancer test deal.
newsitem.headline: Mentor says in bladder cancer test deal.

text.p: Mentor Corp said Tuesday it agreed to be the marketing partner for a new bladder cancer test that it hopes to bring to market this fall.

"Mentor has reached an agreement with Perimmune whereby Mentor will be the exclusive worldwide marketing partner for a new bladder cancer test developed and manufactured by Perimmune," Christopher Conway, chief executive and chairman of Mentor, said in remarks to investors at a Piper Jaffray conference here.
The urine test is more sensitive and accurate than others available, Conway said.
Perimmune is a privately held Rockville, Md., company.
"We hope to be on the market this fall" with the Perimmune bladder cancer test, Conway said.
Santa Barbara, Calif.-based Mentor also announced Tuesday that it has agreed to market radioactive seeds for treating prostate cancer that are manufactured by North American Scientific Inc.
Prostate cancer is the most common form of cancer in men in the U.S. and is often treated by removing the gland, which can result in impotence and urinary incontinence.
Prostate seeding involves implanting radioactive seeds smaller than a grain of rice into the prostate, where they kill the cancer before degrading. No incontinence or impotence follows, Conway said.
The therapy is U.S. Food and Drug Administration-approved and may offer a welcome option for many men, he said.

Shares in Mentor were up 1 to 28-3/4 in late trading. The company makes breast implants, liposuction systems, cataract surgery products, penile implants, urinary incontinence treatment devices and other medical products. Revenues in 1996 totalled $177.8 million.
